target_customer: Engineering and DevOps teams that need developers to run infrastructure tasks safely under review
problem: Developers block on DevOps tasks; hoop lets any engineer do DevOps work under supervision, like code review for ops.
business_model: Open source (MIT) gateway with paid enterprise tier adding control plane, approvals and AI analysis

founders.name: Andrios Robert
prior_employers: Second engineer at an unnamed fintech that reached Series B
education: Computer Science degree, school not named (YC page)

competitors.name: Teleport
competitors.what: Infrastructure access gateway named by hoop as its main comparison

technical_complexity.rationale: Protocol-level proxying of databases and servers with data masking and review workflows is standard but non-trivial engineering for a solo founder.

defensibility.rationale: MIT-licensed open source core and a crowded access-management space; integration depth gives some stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; later positioned as a free Teleport alternative and pivoted messaging to AI agent control.

market_need_then: Developer access to production databases and servers was a known pain; no dated 2021 demand source was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Blunt, confident, lowercase brand name aimed at security and engineering practitioners

rebrands.why: Company calls it a fresh identity with the same team; Runops reached end of life June 1, 2024

branding.community_and_virality: A Hacker News thread comment suggested hoop as a lightweight Teleport replacement; single anecdote

brand_strength.rationale: Small developer brand with open source presence and one rebrand; little independent press on the brand.

pivots.from: Runops terminal tool for database and server work with Slack review
pivots.to: hoop.dev gateway, later framed as runtime control for AI agents
pivots.why: Company describes a revamp with a new identity and enhanced capabilities

outcome_analysis: hoop.dev started as Runops, a code review style tool for DevOps tasks by a solo YC founder, and stayed small for years before a rebrand in 2024 and a first announced seed round in October 2025 led by Venture Guides. It remains active and has repositioned toward controlling AI agents, with no shutdown or acquisition news found.
notes: Business Wire page returned 403 when fetched; the round is known from search result snippets of the release and Pulse 2 and SaaS News coverage. CB Insights lists 1.13M USD over three rounds, unverified. Another aggregator lists a 5M seed for a company named Hoop, likely a different company. Teleport has no dated source from the batch year; its existence in 2021 is not verified here. The Runops name is from hoop.dev's own blog; Product Hunt page was rate limited.
